Present with proofs for the ordered case (route pending): sentence 1~2 with probability p, arithmetization and its uniqueness, the literal encoding with a proof that it fails, the corrected encoding, representation lemma (0.9 L), upper limit (C=3), log-residue formula, sentence A, Compton-Henson-Shelah nonconvergence with a complete proof, example u=3. Gaps: (1) Source section 12 (p.24) claims, in outline, nonconvergence for the unordered G(n,n^{-1/4}) by almost sure encoding: each R_u behaves like an independent random ternary relation of density 1-e^{-1}; +, *, < are almost surely represented for |S|<=ln^{1/3} n; common neighbourhoods N(x1,x2,x3,x4) exist of all sizes up to roughly ln n/ln ln n; BIGGER(S,T) is first-order; a maximal arithmetizable N(x1..x4) has size Theta(ln^{1/3} n); and the sentence 'log |N(x1..x4)| is 1..20 mod 40' is nonconvergent. The handbook (proofboundary def:p03-w03-p03-071-sparse-outline, body 351-383) proves only (1-1/n)^{n-4} -> e^{-1} and sizes up to ln n/(20 ln ln n) (thm:p03-w03-p03-071-all-sizes), states the rest without proof, and records that the literal symmetric relations cannot represent < or +. Owed: exact hypotheses and a complete proof of the G(n,n^{-1/4}) nonconvergence claim (with a repaired encoding), including the all-sizes claim up to roughly ln n/ln ln n, or a proved failure boundary. (2) Source section 12 (p.23) states that with further technical work (perhaps modifying the bound on u) every ternary, even k-ary, relation R could almost surely be represented, and that once {1,...,u} is arithmetized one can say that u is prime or a Fermat prime. Neither the claim nor these examples appear in the handbook treatment (body 204-258). Owed: the claim with exact hypotheses and a complete proof, or an explicit statement that it is not established, and the expressibility examples.
